decor.text: Tobin the hedge-clipper sat down here to rest in the spring. He meant to finish the south row after supper. The hedge finished first.
A faded ribbon is tied to the branch. Every year someone ties a new one beside it. Nobody in Hedgefoot will say whose they are.
We stacked the crates here to hold the thorns back. The thorns did not mind the crates. Go back the way you came.
Two hundred and eleven scratches on this wall, in rows of five. Then the scratches stop, and one clean line runs across all of them.
The mason left his tools and his lunch on the ledge. The lunch is long gone to dust. Nothing has been taken, and nothing has been finished.
A bedroll, a cold fire, a diary. The last page says: I can hear the walls humming the song my mother used to sing. I am going to listen a little closer.
Honey for the lamp and wax for the wick. Mind the floor here. It is sweet, and it is not always honey.
Even the guards of the comb grow old. This one stood so long the wax grew over his boots. He has not been relieved.
It is quiet here. The cells are shut and warm. Whatever sleeps in them has not been told it is time.
I came for one perfect shell. This is the fortieth, and it is still not perfect. I will stay a little longer.
The tide has not come here in a hundred years, yet the floor is always damp. Leave a coin or leave a word. Do not leave nothing.
I hid my pearls under the third tile. Whoever you are, the third tile is loose and the pearls are paste. I knew you would look.
Scratched: We took turns at the lamp. Then there was only one of us to take a turn.
Chalked: The left way is shorter. The right way is kinder.
A scrap of cloth: If you find my boot, keep it. I will not be needing the other.
Carved: Water here, three days behind me. Do not drink the second pool.
Scratched: I heard footsteps behind me for an hour. They stopped when I stopped. They are still there.
Chalked: Rested here. Nothing came. I mean to say so in the towns, and nobody will believe me.
Written small: Counted forty turns since the last sign. Turned back at forty-one.
Scratched: Dear Mara, I have found the middle. It is smaller than we thought.
Chalked: The wall is warm on this side. I did not look at the other side.
Carved: Someone has been here before me and left the lamp lit. I thank them. I do not see them.
A note, pinned: Sorry about the mess. I was in a hurry to leave.
Scratched: Good ground for a camp, if you like the sound of the dripping. I have stopped hearing it.
Chalked: Brother, if you read this, go home. I mean it kindly.
Carved: The roots push the stones out every spring. By autumn the maze is a little different.
Scratched: Quiet. Too quiet for the Hollow. I went the other way.
A child's hand: I WAS HERE AND IT WAS FINE.
Chalked: Two ways out. I took the one that did not smell of honey.
Scratched: A gold coin under the loose stone. I put it back. It looked at me.
Written in charcoal: Turn back, or at least turn on the lamp.
Carved: I do not know where I am, but I have never been so sure of the way.
Scratched: The hedge grew a hand's width while I wrote this.
Chalked: Shells under the lamp, a candle in the dust. Somebody lived here, and not so long ago.
A note: The treasure is not here. I looked. Do not look again.
Scratched: The pearls in the wall are real. The wall wants them back.
Chalked: I buried my sword here. The maze has taken enough of it already.
Carved: My name is Pell. I was a tinker. If you find the cart, it is yours.
Scratched: The air changes here, a little sweeter, a little colder. Go slowly.
Chalked: Stopped here to mend my boot. Lost an hour. Lost the way. Found this note instead.
Written small: The dead end is not the end. Nor is it the way.
Scratched: One more turn, I said. One more turn.

decor.txt: GENERAL GOODS. Marl, of Hedgefoot. Everything for the road into the maze.
GENERAL GOODS. Dwen, of Cairnhold. Chalk marks cost extra. Getting lost costs more.
GENERAL GOODS. Sela, of Combwick. The honey is free if you buy the bread.
GENERAL GOODS. Pearla, of Nacre Landing. Salted, dried and shelled, all of it.
GENERAL GOODS. Hask, of Dunewell. Water is by the cup. Do not ask for a second cup.
GENERAL GOODS. Ilse, of Blue Lantern. Open until the last lamp goes out, which is never.
GENERAL GOODS. Tomm, of Tessera. Anything you need, and some things you do not.
GENERAL GOODS. Orbin, of Gildmere. Gold only. And it must be real gold, we check.
WEAPONSMITH. Brand, of Hedgefoot. Shears sold as shears, swords sold as swords. Please do not confuse the two.
ARMOURER. Gunnar, of Hedgefoot. Hedge-green plate. Hard to spot and hard to hit.
MAGIC SELLER. Syl, of Hedgefoot. Scrolls, rings and a little hedge sage. Ask me nothing about the sage.
GENERAL TRADER. Pim, of Hedgefoot. Rope, torches and bread. Slugs not included.
INN. Mother Tansy, of Hedgefoot. Clean beds, warm soup and a hedge to hide behind.
WEAPONSMITH. Hild, of Cairnhold. Stone-ground edges that outlast the stone.
ARMOURER. Sigrun, of Cairnhold. Heavy as a cairn, and nearly as hard to knock over.
MAGIC SELLER. Orrin, of Cairnhold. Cold stone charms. They hum when someone lies to you.
GENERAL TRADER. Sabel, of Cairnhold. Chalk, rope and one good strong lantern.
INN. Old Garrick, of Cairnhold. Stone walls a yard thick. Nothing comes through, including the noise.
WEAPONSMITH. Ketter, of Combwick. Wax-polished blades. They slide out clean and slide in cleaner.
ARMOURER. Aldric, of Combwick. Honeycomb mail: light, strong and faintly sticky.
MAGIC SELLER. Vesper, of Combwick. Honey draughts and sweet charms. Stir well, drink slowly.
GENERAL TRADER. Tobb, of Combwick. Comb honey, candles and spare wicks.
INN. Big Hesper, of Combwick. Honey on the porridge, honey on the pillow, honey on the cat.
WEAPONSMITH. Osk, of Nacre Landing. Pearl-handled and slug-tested.
ARMOURER. Edda, of Nacre Landing. Shell plate, polished daily by someone who should be doing something else.
MAGIC SELLER. Mirel, of Nacre Landing. Tide charms and pearl rings. Mind the pearls, they watch.
GENERAL TRADER. Wren, of Nacre Landing. Salt, kelp and dry socks. You will want the socks.
INN. Little Joss, of Nacre Landing. Beds shaped like shells. Please do not curl up in one and get carried off.
WEAPONSMITH. Varn, of Dunewell. Dry steel, never a speck of rust. We have no water to rust it.
ARMOURER. Rolf, of Dunewell. Sand-hardened leather for people who like walking out alive.
MAGIC SELLER. Quill, of Dunewell. Dust of the old dunes in little jars. It is mostly dust.
GENERAL TRADER. Cask, of Dunewell. Water skins, dates and sand boots.
INN. Marta, of Dunewell. The coolest cellar in the maze, and the only cool thing in Dunewell.
WEAPONSMITH. Mara, of Blue Lantern. Blades that flash blue by lamplight. Very good for morale.
ARMOURER. Tilde, of Blue Lantern. Blue-steel helms. Dents mended free, bad dents for a small fee.
MAGIC SELLER. Anwen, of Blue Lantern. Blue-lamp charms, brightest in the dark and bad at everything else.
GENERAL TRADER. Nell, of Blue Lantern. Lamp oil by the pint, wicks by the yard.
INN. Ferris, of Blue Lantern. A lamp in every window and a bed beneath every lamp.
WEAPONSMITH. Dagny, of Tessera. Every edge set like a tile: true, flat and level.
ARMOURER. Bram, of Tessera. Plate with a mosaic trim. Dying in style is still dying, so please do not.
MAGIC SELLER. Lorn, of Tessera. Glass-bead charms, a different colour for each problem.
GENERAL TRADER. Harl, of Tessera. Tile glue, nails and a great deal of string.
INN. Dame Orla, of Tessera. Mosaic headboards. Count the tiles till you fall asleep.
WEAPONSMITH. Tor, of Gildmere. Gilded hilts, honest edges.
ARMOURER. Hedda, of Gildmere. Gold-leaf cuirasses. Not for the thrifty, not for the slug.
MAGIC SELLER. Isolde, of Gildmere. Gilded rings and gilded staves. Gold outside, magic inside.
GENERAL TRADER. Dorrit, of Gildmere. Fine bread, fine cheese, fine prices.
INN. Cob, of Gildmere. Gilded beds, plain porridge.
THE CHURCH OF HEDGEFOOT. The roof is a hedge, and it leaks only in spring. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF CAIRNHOLD. A stone stands by the door for every one the maze kept. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF COMBWICK. The candles are beeswax and the sermons are short. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF NACRE LANDING. The font is a shell the size of a bath. Please do not use it as one. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF DUNEWELL. We pray for rain. We have for forty years, and we are patient. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF BLUE LANTERN. The light never goes out, and neither does the priest. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF TESSERA. Every tile in the floor is a prayer. Please do not stand on the loud ones. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.
THE CHURCH OF GILDMERE. Gold on the altar, patches on the roof. The gold is not for sale. Healing, mending and a quiet prayer, for a small gift.

NOTICES OF HEDGEFOOT. Lost: one pair of shears, blue handle. Answers to nothing. Wanted: someone to tell the hedge it is not a door. The slugs have been seen on the lower path. They have not been seen leaving.

THE ROAD FROM HEDGEFOOT. Combwick: north-west, about 65 squares. Nacre Landing: north-west, about 86 squares. Cairnhold: west, about 95 squares. The Great Atrium: north, about 167 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF CAIRNHOLD. Lost: a small grey stone, very dear to me. Wanted: a mason who can carve a door that stays where it is put. The cairn is full. Please leave your stone beside it, not on it.

THE ROAD FROM CAIRNHOLD. Combwick: north-east, about 57 squares. Dunewell: north, about 82 squares. Nacre Landing: north-east, about 89 squares. The Great Atrium: north-east, about 176 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF COMBWICK. Lost: one jar of honey, dark. The finder may keep half. Wanted: a beekeeper with a steady hand and a short memory. The honey press is not a ride.

THE ROAD FROM COMBWICK. Nacre Landing: north, about 36 squares. Dunewell: north-west, about 50 squares. Cairnhold: south-west, about 57 squares. The Great Atrium: north, about 128 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF NACRE LANDING. Lost: a pearl, lightly used. Wanted: someone to row the ferry, and someone to tell them where it goes. Please stop wishing aloud at the fountain. It gets crowded.

THE ROAD FROM NACRE LANDING. Dunewell: west, about 36 squares. Combwick: south, about 36 squares. Blue Lantern: north-west, about 74 squares. The Great Atrium: north, about 92 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF DUNEWELL. Lost: a cup of water. Reward: a cup of water. Wanted: one honest well-digger. Thirsty ones preferred. The water ration is unchanged. So is our opinion of it.

THE ROAD FROM DUNEWELL. Nacre Landing: east, about 36 squares. Blue Lantern: north, about 47 squares. Combwick: south-east, about 50 squares. The Great Atrium: north-east, about 97 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.

NOTICES OF BLUE LANTERN. Lost: a blue lamp, still lit, last seen walking away. Wanted: a third lamplighter who gets on with the first two. If your lamp goes out, light it again. Do not wait for us. We are not coming.

THE ROAD FROM BLUE LANTERN. Dunewell: south, about 47 squares. Nacre Landing: south-east, about 74 squares. Combwick: south, about 97 squares. The Great Atrium: north-east, about 79 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF TESSERA. Lost: tile number 1,204, blue, with a small chip. Wanted: a steady hand for the big mosaic. Steady, I said. Please do not step on the loud tiles.

THE ROAD FROM TESSERA. Gildmere: south-east, about 25 squares. Nacre Landing: south-west, about 96 squares. Blue Lantern: west, about 97 squares. The Great Atrium: west, about 21 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
NOTICES OF GILDMERE. Lost: one gold leaf, nearly weightless. It may be on you. Wanted: a buyer for a very shiny statue. The ember warden is not for hugging.

THE ROAD FROM GILDMERE. Tessera: north-west, about 25 squares. Nacre Landing: south-west, about 99 squares. Blue Lantern: west, about 116 squares. The Great Atrium: west, about 46 squares. The maze does not run in straight lines, so walk with patience.
THE GARDENER'S REST. Here stands Orrin Hedge, who trimmed the hedge of Hedgefoot for forty years. He was last seen trimming it from the inside. We think he is still at it.

THE BELL OF THE LOST. Ring once for every one the maze has kept. It has been rung 211 times. The rope wore through, so we ring it with a spoon. A scratch beside the bell says: the cairn pays its tithe to whoever kneels at the bell.
THE HONEY PRESS. Sticky, loud and strictly no tasting. A smaller notice beneath says: whoever tasted is still stuck.
THE PEARL FOUNTAIN. Throw one coin for luck. The keeper collects on Thursdays, whatever day it is.
THE OLD WELL. Forty fathoms deep. Do not drop anything you want back, and do not drop anything you do not. A mark by the stones says: look below the second crate.
THE LAMPLIGHTERS' POST. Two lamplighters, one ladder and forty years of disagreement. The ladder is winning.
THE MOSAIC CORNER. The great mosaic was smashed on this spot. The tile-trader has the pieces he can find. He is looking for the rest, and for whatever did it.
THE GILDER'S BENCH. Everything here is gold leaf. Please do not lick it. The Gilder has had complaints. A bead of gold behind the bench is a gift, if you are quick.
SILENCE NOTICE. Silence is kept in this room by order of the Warden. Anyone caught whispering will be shushed by the clock.
THE LAMPLIGHTER'S PLAQUE. Tuck the Lamplighter lit these lamps himself, one a night, to see how long the dark would let him. It is still letting him.
A FROG'S WARNING. The water is clean and the frogs are rude. Please do not ask the frogs for directions. They will give them.
READING ROOM RULES. Most of the books here are about the maze. One is about cheese. The cheese one is the most worn.
TEA NOTICE. Rest Stop. Free sitting, cheap tea, no questions. Please wash your own cup. The cups are all the same cup.
DO NOT WAKE. Please do not wake the sleeper. He has been here three days. We checked. He is asleep. He snores in the key of the corridor.
LANTERN LANDING RULE. Lost lamps end up here. Leave one, take one. Do not take the one that is still warm. It belongs to someone.
MOSSY CORNER. The moss here has been growing since before the maze. Please do not pet it. It has started to purr.
THE WAITING CARD. The Waiting Room. For whom, nobody remembers. A card on the table says: back in five minutes. The card is old.
A TORN JOURNAL. Day 9. Safe here. Day 10. Still safe. Day 11. Very hungry, but safe. Day 12. Found a box under the crates. The box was not empty. Neither am I.

decor.pbt: Carved under the owl: It keeps what the dark gives it. Take a little, and leave the rest. It counts.
Day nineteen. The Dry Ward goes round in circles. I have decided it is the corridors that are wrong and not me. If you read this, I went left.
DUNEWELL. Founded beside a well. The well turned out to be a rumour. We kept the name out of stubbornness.
Tuck lit forty lamps here, one a night. She lit the last one, put down her ladder and went home. The statue is her. The lamp is still lit. Do not blow it out.
Waiting for the Blue Door to open since spring. The bench is very good. The door is not.
INKWELL COURT ARCHIVE. Everything is filed. Nothing can be found. Please return books to the shelf they fell from.
Counting the tiles. Lost count at 3,112. Starting again from the beginning. Please do not talk to me.
We stacked all this against the worm. The worm was behind us the whole time. It is a very good barricade.
Grout Court was to have a fine floor by Friday. The mason promised. It is still Friday here, and he is still kneeling in the corner.
GILDMERE HUNT CLUB. Trophies so far: 3 antlers and 1 boot. Slugs: none. They know why.
A coin for the road and a chest for the patient. Not all that glitters is gold, but this is. Mind the lid.
Someone leaves a candle here every week. Nobody has ever seen them. Please leave it burning.

Scratched: I came all this way for a dead end. It is a nice one, I will say that.
Chalked: Turn back. There is nothing here but this note, and I wrote it myself.
